blueprint.ending_payoff: Back in the quiet room from the opening: the faint tone the microphone caught is now understood as the sound of the ear's amplifier at work, the ring Gold warned of in 1948, so the viewer leaves hearing their own hearing as something their body does, and knowing that in us the cells doing it are not replaced.

beats.experience: Intrigued disbelief: a microphone in a silent room records a tone from inside a person's ear with no speaker anywhere. The question 'where did that come from?' is planted and held on purpose until B05.
beats.visual_intent: An ordinary quiet room and a screen with one sharp peak; the picture holds still so the viewer listens, and the source of the sound is not explained.

beats.experience: Wonder at the scale: the viewer realises how faint, how loud and how finely tuned their own hearing is, and feels the puzzle that a small coil of fluid could manage it.
beats.visual_intent: The pea-sized coil beside a pea, then unrolled into a strip laid along a keyboard; a magnifier compares the membrane's movement with an atom, so the scale is seen rather than stated.

beats.experience: The click of a clever idea: a young physicist sees a radio receiver in the ear, and the viewer is handed a testable consequence, that too much feedback would make the ear ring.
beats.visual_intent: Gold at a 1940s desk beside an opened radio set and a sketch of the ear; then a chalkboard sequence: a wave dying in thick fluid, held up by added energy, and spilling out as a ring when the boost is too strong.

significance.matters_because: It turns the puzzle of B02 into a claim that could be checked: if the ear adds energy to what it hears, a healthy ear might give some of it back as sound, so the viewer now has something to wait for.
significance.reward: The pleasure of an idea from radio engineering suddenly fitting the ear, and a prediction to watch.

depends_on.what: the puzzle: a coil of damping fluid that should not be able to hear so faintly or so sharply

beats.experience: A slow deflation: the idea is set aside for thirty years, partly through the opposition of Georg von Bekesy, whose own work held the field's attention, and its author leaves for the stars; the viewer starts to wonder whether he was simply wrong.
beats.visual_intent: A worn 1940s folder on a library shelf as the light changes across the years; a window onto a starry night sky. Time passes in the picture while the words move on.

beats.experience: 'So that's what it was': the opening's sound is explained, and an ignored idea is proved right by listening to the ear itself.
beats.visual_intent: A late-1970s lab: a click goes in and a smaller echo returns on the oscilloscope; then the opening room's screen comes back and Gold's predicted ring is laid over its peak, the two shapes meeting.

significance.matters_because: It answers the mystery the film opened with and pays Gold's warning from B03: the ear does ring, so it cannot be a passive receiver, and thirty years of neglect end in a measurement made on ordinary ears.
significance.reward: The relief of an answer and the satisfaction of a vindicated prediction, heard rather than only told.

depends_on.what: the unexplained tone recorded in a silent room
Gold's warning that too much feedback would make the ear ring
the idea's thirty years of neglect

beats.experience: Fascination at the machinery: the amplifier is a single cell that stretches and shrinks thousands of times a second, driven by a protein named for speed, and in mice without that protein hearing falls away.
beats.visual_intent: A magnified outer hair cell drawn at three lengths; a wall of tiny identical proteins changing shape together; two mice side by side with very different hearing bars.

beats.experience: Honest curiosity: even now, nobody is sure exactly what sets the ring going, and the viewer is let in on a live question.
beats.visual_intent: The hair cell with two question marks, one on its body and one on its tuft of hairs, and a frog in the corner as the animal in which the tuft was seen moving on its own.

hedges.R6: Nobody is yet sure exactly what starts the ring: the stretching cell itself, or the little tuft of hairs on top of it, which in frogs has been seen moving on its own.

beats.experience: A personal stake: in us, hair cells lost to noise do not come back, though birds regrow theirs; and the ear's own echo has become a way to test it.
beats.visual_intent: Neat rows of hair cells seen from above with a flattened gap beside a loudspeaker shape; a songbird with its rows complete again; a clothed adult sitting upright in a clinic chair with a small probe in the ear and an echo trace on a screen.

beats.experience: Quiet awe: hearing is something the viewer's ears do with their own energy, and the faint sound from the opening is the sound of that work.
beats.visual_intent: The opening room again at dusk: the same person, no probe now, listening, with a soft glow at the ear; the peak from B01 is now read as the trace of a working amplifier.

significance.matters_because: It changes what the viewer thinks hearing is, from sound arriving to work their own cells do, and turns the opening's mystery tone into a sign of that work, which in us is not replaced once lost.
significance.reward: A quiet sense of awe at an everyday act, and a reason to care for it.
